title: Tenant surge attenuator and transparent failover during customer escalations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a recent customer escalation we observed tenant-localized spikes that produced cascading 5xx errors and long tail timeouts. Retries from SDKs amplified the load causing KV cache churn and head-node saturation. This ticket implements a Tenant Surge Attenuator (TSA) — a small, tenant-scoped admission controller + transparent failover policy that reduces retry amplification and provides a safe fallback path for customer traffic during escalations.

Problem details: repeated bursts from a tenant led to: 1) backend task queue growth; 2) synchronous retries originating from language SDKs and orchestrators; 3) KV cache eviction storms that increased cold-path GPU work; 4) elevated 5xx and client-visible timeouts. Existing circuit breakers and backpressure were too coarse-grained (service-wide) and did not provide tenant-level containment or graceful result alternatives.

Goal: deploy a minimal-surface change that reduces customer-visible 5xx/timeouts during tenant surges while preserving correctness and traceability for post-incident analysis. Solutions must be reversible and tested on staging with synthetic tenant burst traffic.
acceptance_criteria: TSA gate implemented in edge router with tenant-scoped leaky-bucket admission
Automatic transparent fallback to cached or quantized model variant for affected requests
SDK retry policy guidance aligned with server-side 429/503 hints and documented in SDK repo
End-to-end synthetic test shows 70% reduction in client-visible 5xx for simulated tenant surge
Telemetry dashboards updated: per-tenant 5xx rate, queue depth, KV cache hit-rate, and retry amplification metric
Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation and customer communication templates
tasks: Add tenant leaky-bucket admission to edge proxy (rate + burst + cooldown)
Expose tenant health signal to routing layer (healthy/degraded/quarantine)
Implement transparent fallback: serve from prefix cache or lower-cost model variant when tenant flagged
Instrument retry-amplification metric (client retries per original request) and KV churn metric
Tune server-side circuit breakers to return explicit guidance headers (X-Backoff, Retry-After, X-Fallback-Allowed)
Coordinate SDK team: publish backoff guidance and a small SDK patch to respect server hints
Create e2e staging job that replays recorded escalation traffic against TSA and collects SLO metrics
Draft customer-facing incident explanation and postmortem checklist
comments: 2025-11-03 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after post-incident triage. Root cause points to tenant-localized surge + retry amplification. Proposed short-term containment and medium-term circuit improvements.

2025-11-04 - Diego Morales: Investigation notes attached. Edge router can admit tenant tags; prototype leaky-bucket live in staging-ops branch. Initial load test shows decreased queue growth but increases cache miss rate by 12%.

2025-11-06 - Riley Chen (SRE): Observed that KV cache compaction correlates with set of long-running requests; adding soft-eviction reduced cold-path hop count. Suggested transparent fallback to cached completions for specific endpoints (completions/streaming).
2025-11-08 - Product (Maya Singh): Customer comms draft reviewed. Need to ensure fallbacks are opt-in per tenant for enterprise contracts.

2025-11-10 - Diego Morales: Implemented X-Fallback-Allowed header and server-side decision doc at https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RINF/TSA-Design. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/498
2025-11-12 - QA (Jordan Park): Staging e2e shows client-visible 5xx down 74% for synthetic tenant burst at 3x baseline. Two flaky tests around streaming resume to investigate.
2025-11-14 - Diego Morales: Hotfix branch for SDK guidance created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1320. Need legal sign-off before auto-enabling fallback for enterprise-tenants.
2025-11-15 - Asha Patel: Marking In Progress -> focusing on rollout plan and observing staging for additional 48 hours before canary in production.
notes_for_oncall: If high-traffic tenant triggers quarantine, avoid global circuit trips — TSA should contain the traffic.
When serving fallback, set X-Redwood-Fallback: true header so logs are searchable.
Follow postmortem template: link to incident dashboard and include timeline of SDK retries vs server-side throttles.
